react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this treatment-vs-control metabolomics study. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182), Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052) and Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-70171) with FDR values as low as 4.25×10⁻¹¹ and fold-enrichment exceeding 1100 — driven by four input metabolites: sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactinol (C01235) and glycerol (C00116). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as the top hit at p = 3.25×10⁻⁷, matching the same four compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned Galactose Metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 4 (p = 0.00109) with near-complete pathway overlap (12 of 13 compounds), providing orthogonal empirical support. Deoxycytidine, fructose 1-phosphate and D-glucose did not map to the galactose cluster in any tool. The convergence across ORA (hypergeometric), KEGG PSEA and m/z-network ranking — spanning SMPDB, KEGG and MUMM namespaces simultaneously — constitutes a strong consensus finding that the treatment specifically dysregulates galactose catabolism and the associated galactosyl-inositol osmolyte shunt.

Mummichog m/z-network ranking placed MUMM:galactose_metabolism rank 4 (p = 9.24×10⁻⁴, 12 of 13 pathway compounds recovered from the input mass list).
